per_policy_guidance.guidance: Use only as a closely monitored attached-transport option, not as the default. In validation from its own demonstrated entry states, h01 met the fixed final exit in 5/12 runs; successful runs first met it at steps 184–225 and ended with the block inside and drawer_position 0.296–0.300. Its documented intended use is an open, stable drawer with reliable object_pose, closed fingers, two causal frames showing common block/TCP motion, and a feasible arm posture; the object-frame design is appropriate in principle for a plausibly held, displaced block, but displacement benefit has no out-of-distribution rollout evidence. Avoid uncertain attachment, unreliable pose, premature-drop recovery, or post-release/handle motion. The seven validation failures comprised six final outside-cavity states and one inside state with drawer_position 0.205; watch for block/TCP decoupling before the cavity, abrupt relative-pose change, off-cavity settling, drawer_position falling to <=0.26, extreme object motion, or persistent IK/limit diagnostics. After two frames show an inside, floor-height, stationary block detached from the opened gripper, switch to h02 for destination/handle anchoring, or h03 if release phase remains locally ambiguous. Hand close_drawer only that verified deposit state, preferably with the free gripper at the handle approach.

Preferred destination/fixture-anchored choice within the validated distribution. h02 passed 12/12 demonstrated-entry validations; every run ended with the object inside, drawer_position 0.300, and zero IK-unconverged steps, with first exit attainment at steps 198–250. Use when the drawer is open/stable, target_pose is available and rigidly represents the drawer, the block is plausibly held or already over the cavity, and the approach is reachable. It is especially suited by design to alignment, descent, release, retreat, and the fixed handle transition; any benefit under an unseen displaced destination is structural, not rollout-validated. Avoid a missing/jumping target_pose, an attached block far outside demonstrated destination-relative support, a dropped-object recovery state, or infeasible/collision-prone targets. Failure cues are loss of block/TCP following before release, descent outside the cavity, a block still suspended or following after opening, or IK residual/limit warnings. Keep destination anchoring through release and retreat. Transfer to close_drawer only after two causal observations show the block stationary at drawer-floor height and detached; a late handoff can occur with the free gripper at the handle. Use h01 only for a far-displaced but reliably attached transport state, and h03 for local release/retreat ambiguity.

Preferred alternative for near-demonstration, locally perturbed, or phase-ambiguous states. h03 passed 12/12 demonstrated-entry validations; final drawer_position was 0.2988–0.300 with the block inside, all runs had zero IK-unconverged steps, and first exit attainment was at steps 189–268. Use with an open/stable drawer, valid object/target observations and joints, and a block either plausibly attached for carry or visible in the demonstrated cavity/release corridor. Its fresh-TCP local corrections and carry/release/retreat/handle phase prior target local lag, height, or release-timing ambiguity, not large global displacement. Avoid large object or destination shifts, noisy settling, unseen drops, or recovery states; there is no out-of-distribution result. Suspect failure if inferred phase conflicts with observed block/TCP motion, the block separates before the cavity, opening occurs outside it, the block follows after opening, local increments repeatedly grow/drift, or IK reports nonconvergence/limits. Do not use the auxiliary phase class alone to authorize handoff. Preserve two-frame history and transfer to close_drawer only when actual geometry shows a stationary floor-height block detached from the TCP, preferably after retreat/handle approach. Choose h01 for reliably attached displaced transport or h02 for destination displacement and fixture-anchored completion.

Experimental/specialized, not a default: h04 passed only 5/12 validations from its own demonstrated entry states. Use, if at all, with strict external monitoring when object_pose and target_pose are reliable, the drawer is open/stable, the block is plausibly held close to the TCP, and a coherent close-to-separated transition is expected. Its proximity-gated object-to-destination frame is intended to combine attached transport with fixture-anchored retreat, but no out-of-distribution benefit was observed. In the five passes, first exit attainment was at steps 172–221 and final drawer_position was 0.277–0.300. Four of the seven failed runs transiently met the exit but then closed the drawer with the block inside; those runs had full-task success but violated this skill’s required open-drawer exit. The other three ended with the object outside and drawer_position <=0.083. Thus do not treat a transient in-cavity event as durable: stop or hand off promptly once two frames confirm an inside, floor-height, stationary, detached block while drawer_position remains >0.26. Avoid noisy/chattering object–TCP distance, uncertain attachment, premature drops, or unreachable targets. Watch for reference-weight collapse while the block should be held, weight persistence/chatter after release, opening outside the cavity, a block above floor height or following retreat, drawer closure before handoff, and IK/limit warnings. Switch to h02 once separated/deposited, h03 for near-nominal release ambiguity, and invoke close_drawer only after observed stationarity and separation.

summary: The only evidence is in-distribution validation from each policy’s own training-segment entry state in the 12 demonstrations, run for 720 steps and scored at the final state by: block inside the cavity and drawer_position >0.26. There is no out-of-distribution result, so the displacement/phase advantages described by the priors must not be presented as observed robustness. On this protocol, h02 and h03 are the strongest choices (12/12 each, with zero IK-unconverged steps); select h02 for destination/fixture anchoring and h03 for local phase or release ambiguity. h01 and h04 each passed 5/12 and should be reserved for their documented specialized attached-transport conditions with active failure monitoring and prompt switching. The placement exit deliberately leaves the drawer open: h02/h03 validation passes therefore did not constitute full-task success. Conversely, four h04 runs completed the full task by closing the drawer but failed this placement skill’s open-drawer exit. Across policies, authorize close_drawer only from two-frame evidence that the object is inside, at floor height, stationary, and detached; preserve causal history at the switch. None of the policies is validated for dropped-object recovery, unreachable targets, collision-clearance violations, or unseen pose distributions.
